title: Session-aware latency SLO and staged deprecation rollout playbook
creator: Elena Garcia
description: Purpose: Define a session-aware SLO matrix, error-budget calculations, and an operational rollout + deprecation playbook for model/runtime variants. Scope: hosted API (chat + streaming) and Dedicated. Exclude on-prem private deployments for initial rollout (will follow with a separate PRD). Background: incidents in Q4 2025 showed p99 tail regressions for long-lived conversations when batching and KV cache thrashing occurred. This ticket consolidates requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout gates, and deprecation steps to retire older runtime kernels and a legacy quantized variant without customer disruption. Key decisions to capture: how we classify sessions, measurement surface (edge latency vs service-first-byte vs end-to-end), per-tenant vs global SLOs, canary cadence, and automated rollback triggers.
session_classification: Short: <=8 user messages in session (interactive, low context)
Medium: 9-200 user messages (sustained conversations, typical chat apps)
Long: >200 user messages (sessions with heavy context and long histories)
proposed_slos: Short sessions: p95 first-byte <= 120ms, p99 first-byte <= 350ms
Medium sessions: p95 first-byte <= 200ms, p99 first-byte <= 600ms
Long sessions: p95 first-byte <= 350ms, p99 first-byte <= 1500ms
Availability (hosted API): 99.95% monthly across all models and regions (excludes scheduled maintenance windows)
Error budget: monthly budget = 1 - availability target; tracked as minute-level burn rate with automatic alerts
measurement_and_instrumentation: Primary metric: service-first-byte (SFB) measured at gateway ingress to isolate runtime and infra effects
Secondary metric: end-to-end p95/p99 (client-observed) for regression correlation
Tagging: all traces and metrics must be annotated by session_id, tenant_id (if present), model_variant, kernel_version, and queueing_latency
Dashboards: add 'session-length breakdown' chart and 'p99 delta vs baseline' panel in Console under release-2026-q2-slos
rollout_gates: Canary stage 1: 1% production traffic for 48 hours. Gate: no p99 regression > 8% relative (or >100ms absolute) and no sustained error-rate increase that would consume >10% of monthly error budget
Canary stage 2: 5% traffic for 72 hours. Gate: burn rate <= 2x, p99 regression <= 5% relative
Ramp: 25% for 72 hours, then 100% after monitoring window of 7 days provided burn rate <1.25x
Automated rollback: trigger if during any gate burn rate > 5x for 30 minutes or p99 increases by >20% absolute
Safety nets: route new sessions to fallback model_variant (last-known-good) for 3xx of requests when kernel fails, with automatic incident ticket creation
deprecation_playbook: Announce deprecation 30 days before removal on status page and in-console banner for affected tenants
Maintain compatibility fallback for 90 days after deprecation announcement: traffic will be routed to legacy variant only if automatic fallback is triggered
Provide migration guide: performance expectations, recommended quantized variant, and SDK example for setting model_variant pinning
Blockers that pause deprecation: any month where aggregated tenant opt-out > 5% or a critical bug found in migration path
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: metrics and charts exist in Console; session-length breakdown and SFB panels show live data for all regions
Automated gating: canary controller enforces gates and can automatically rollback according to rules above
Documentation: PRD + migration guide published in Confluence with examples and customer communication templates
Testing: canary rollout executed in pre-prod and a staged canary executed in prod without violating error-budget based gates in two independent test runs
Compliance: release notes include explicit note about availability targets and deprecation timeline for partners and Dedicated customers
